audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-023): A malicious block proposer MUST NOT be able to set a future timestamp for MEV advantages
audit_items.state_context: slots.StartTime uses genesis time (fixed at genesis, stored in beacon state) and current slot (set by ProcessSlots before block processing, not proposer-controlled). SecondsPerSlot is a network constant. The timestamp is deterministically computed from these fixed parameters.

phase1.summary: The timestamp validation in ValidatePayload enforces strict equality between payload.Timestamp() and slots.StartTime(st.GenesisTime(), st.Slot()). The genesis time is fixed at genesis and stored in beacon state. The slot is set by ProcessSlots before block processing runs, so it is not proposer-influenced. SecondsPerSlot is a network-wide constant. No mutable or attacker-influenced intermediate variable exists between state's slot value and the computed expected timestamp. StartTime uses integer arithmetic with overflow protection via SafeMul. No TOCTOU vulnerability exists as state processing is single-threaded per block with copy-on-write semantics.

phase2.summary: An attacker (block proposer) controls payload.Timestamp(). The check is payload.Timestamp() != uint64(t.Unix()) where t is computed from network-fixed parameters. No tolerance band, no off-by-one window, no alternative code path. Proposer setting timestamp != expected value receives ErrInvalidPayloadTimeStamp. Delay-based attacks are ineffective because the required timestamp is anchored to slot number, not wall clock.
attack_scenarios: Proposer sets timestamp = expected + 1: Fails validation, block rejected with ErrInvalidPayloadTimeStamp
Proposer sets timestamp to current wall clock: Only passes if wall clock == slot time, which is the intended behavior; no MEV advantage possible since the required timestamp IS the slot time
Proposer delays propagation to use different timestamp: Not possible — required timestamp for the slot is fixed and not wall-clock dependent

phase2_5.reachability_notes: ValidatePayload is called from ProcessPayload which is called from the state transition. P2P-received blocks are attacker-controlled entry points. The validation correctly rejects any timestamp deviation.

phase3.summary: The invariant payload.Timestamp == compute_timestamp_at_slot(state, state.slot) is directly enforced by an equality guard. The guard covers the attacker-controlled field exactly. StartTime computes expected value using only network constants and validated state slot with no attacker influence. Edge cases: slot=0 returns genesis time (correct); far-future slot overflow guarded by SafeMul.
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. ProcessPayload always calls ValidatePayload. No alternative path skips this check. ProcessBlockHeader validates state.slot before ValidatePayload runs.

phase3_5.reason: Property is correctly enforced by strict equality check. No bypass conditions, no alternative code paths skipping validation, no TOCTOU, no concurrency issues. An attacker cannot set a timestamp deviating from compute_timestamp_at_slot without block rejection.
phase3_5.recommendation: No change needed. Implementation correctly satisfies the specification.

audit_items.reasoning: Full 3-phase adversarial analysis completed. The timestamp enforcement in ValidatePayload is a strict equality check anchored to network-fixed parameters (genesis time + slot * SecondsPerSlot). No MEV advantage via timestamp manipulation is possible.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-023): A proposer MUST NOT be able to construct a block that inflates bloom filter and receipt processing overhead
audit_items.state_context: logs_bloom field follows two deserialization paths: (1) REST API: bytesutil.DecodeHexWithLength enforces exactly 256 bytes. (2) P2P gossip: SSZ schema defines LogsBloom as fixed-size Bytes256 (2048-bit bloom filter), enforced by the SSZ deserializer. ValidatePayload does not perform independent size validation — it delegates to the schema/deserialization layer.

phase1.summary: logs_bloom size enforcement operates at two deserialization boundaries. REST API: DecodeHexWithLength(LogsBloomLength=256) enforces exact 256-byte length. P2P: SSZ schema defines logs_bloom as fixed-size Bytes256 vector, enforced by ssz deserializer before any application code runs. ValidatePayload does not independently validate logs_bloom size, relying on schema enforcement. No in-memory path allows construction of oversized logs_bloom in production code paths.

phase2.summary: To inflate bloom filter beyond 256 bytes, attacker must bypass SSZ fixed-size schema (P2P) or DecodeHexWithLength (REST API). SSZ schema for ExecutionPayload.LogsBloom is Bytes256 (fixed-size vector), meaning the SSZ library rejects payloads where bloom filter is not exactly 256 bytes at deserialization time, before any application-level processing. REST API path enforces exact length at conversion. No viable bypass found.
attack_scenarios: P2P attacker sends SSZ-encoded block with 512-byte logs_bloom: SSZ deserializer fails to decode, block rejected before application code
REST API attacker sends hex-encoded 512-byte logs_bloom: DecodeHexWithLength enforces exact 256 bytes, returns error

phase2_5.reachability_notes: Size enforcement happens at deserialization before any bloom filter processing logic is reached. Both entry points independently enforce the 256-byte constraint.

phase3.summary: logs_bloom size invariant (256 bytes = 2048-bit bloom filter) is enforced at both deserialization boundaries. SSZ schema is the guard for P2P; DecodeHexWithLength is the guard for REST API. All known deserialization entry points enforce the constraint before downstream processing. Internal struct construction (e.g., from trusted local execution engine via engine API) is not attacker-controlled.
phase3.guard_identified: SSZ fixed-size Bytes256 schema for P2P; bytesutil.DecodeHexWithLength(e.LogsBloom, fieldparams.LogsBloomLength) at conversions_block_execution.go REST API boundary
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Sufficient. All attacker-reachable deserialization paths enforce the constraint.

phase3_5.reason: logs_bloom field is correctly size-bounded at both P2P (SSZ schema) and REST API (explicit length check) boundaries. No viable path to inject oversized bloom filter that reaches bloom processing logic.
phase3_5.recommendation: No change needed. Size enforcement is correct at all deserialization boundaries.

audit_items.reasoning: Full 3-phase adversarial analysis completed. Bloom filter inflation attack is blocked at both deserialization boundaries (SSZ schema for P2P, DecodeHexWithLength for REST API). No application-level bloom processing code is reachable with an oversized field.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity (tb-023): Block contents MUST be non-repudiable: the block header's parent_hash, state_root, transactions_root MUST be cryptographically committed and verified
audit_items.state_context: Non-repudiation layered defense: (1) BLS signature over block.HashTreeRoot() commits cryptographically to all fields including full ExecutionPayload (parent_hash, state_root, transactions). (2) ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes checks parent_hash == state.latest_execution_payload_header.block_hash. (3) BeaconBlock state_root is checked by deterministic post-state comparison in ExecuteStateTransitionNoVerifyAnySig. (4) Execution payload state_root and transactions_root validated by execution engine via engine_newPayload (trusted local component).

phase1.summary: Non-repudiation enforced via layered mechanism: BLS block signature over HashTreeRoot (commits to entire block including ExecutionPayload.parent_hash, state_root, transactions). ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes directly checks parent_hash chain linkage. Beacon state_root verified by post-state hash comparison. Execution payload state_root and transactions_root validated by execution engine (engine_newPayload). The execution payload state_root is NOT independently checked at consensus layer — it relies on execution engine as trusted component. This is correct per consensus/execution split architecture.
phase1.architectural_note: Execution payload state_root and transactions_root correctness relies on execution engine (engine_newPayload). Execution engine is a trusted local component not under attacker control in the consensus client threat model.

phase2.summary: To repudiate block contents, an attacker must set incorrect parent_hash, state_root, or transactions_root while having block accepted. parent_hash: directly checked by ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes; incorrect value rejected. BeaconBlock state_root: checked by post-state deterministic comparison; cannot be forged. Execution payload state_root: committed to by BLS signature; execution engine rejects block if doesn't match EVM execution result. transactions_root: committed to by BLS signature (via SSZ HashTreeRoot of transactions list); execution engine validates correctness.
attack_scenarios: Proposer sets incorrect parent_hash: ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes rejects (ErrInvalidPayloadBlockHash)
Proposer sets incorrect EVM state_root: BLS signature commits to value; execution engine (engine_newPayload) returns INVALID; block rejected
Proposer sets incorrect transactions_root (transactions list): SSZ HashTreeRoot of block commits to transactions; execution engine validates transaction execution; block rejected
Proposer sets incorrect beacon state_root: ExecuteStateTransitionNoVerifyAnySig post-state comparison rejects block

phase2_5.reachability_notes: All relevant fields protected by BLS signature over HashTreeRoot. parent_hash additionally checked by ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes. Beacon state_root checked by deterministic post-state verification. Execution payload state_root/transactions_root checked by execution engine.

phase3.summary: Non-repudiation invariant implemented via: (1) BLS signature over block.HashTreeRoot() — covers all block fields including ExecutionPayload. (2) ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes — directly checks parent_hash against chain state. (3) State root equality check in ExecuteStateTransitionNoVerifyAnySig. (4) engine_newPayload (execution engine) validates EVM state_root and transaction correctness. Guards are collectively sufficient. Edge case: pre-merge (IsMergeTransitionComplete=false) correctly skips parent_hash check since execution chain doesn't exist yet.
phase3.guard_identified: BLS signature over HashTreeRoot (cryptographic commitment); ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes (parent_hash linkage); post-state equality check; execution engine validation
phase3.guard_sufficiency: Collectively sufficient. Each field has at least one concrete enforcement mechanism. Execution payload state_root/transactions_root rely on execution engine (trusted local component by design in consensus/execution split architecture).

phase3_5.reason: Non-repudiation is correctly provided by layered mechanisms: BLS signature over full HashTreeRoot (cryptographic commitment to all fields), parent_hash consensus-layer chain linkage verification, beacon state_root deterministic comparison, and execution engine payload validation. No bypass exists for any of these checks under the consensus client threat model.
phase3_5.recommendation: No change needed. Optional: add documentation to ValidatePayloadWhenMergeCompletes clarifying that execution payload state_root and transactions_root are validated by the execution engine, not the consensus layer, to make the trust assumption explicit.

audit_items.reasoning: Full 3-phase adversarial analysis completed. Non-repudiation is enforced via four layered mechanisms. parent_hash is directly checked at consensus layer. state_root and transactions_root are cryptographically committed via BLS signature and verified by execution engine. No bypass path found.
